subject: URGENT: Stellaris AI - private VPC throughput & latency surge, mitigation plan
messages:
From: infra@stellaris.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: ceo@stellaris.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 09:04:12 -0400
Subject: production: p95/p99 latency and 5xx burst on private VPC

Neha —

We started seeing a sharp jump in latency and a correlated spike in 5xx rates on our private VPC cluster at 08:45 UTC. P95 has gone from ~220ms to ~900ms and p99 is off the charts; throughput (QPS) has dropped ~35% as many requests are being retried. The traffic is predominantly inference from the recommendation pipeline (short prompts, streaming disabled).

Attached a small metrics snapshot and recent logs (stellaris_metrics_snapshot_20260621.zip). We're also seeing an uptick in decoder OOM/retry events and queue buildup on the gateway. This is impacting our customer-facing recommendations and a small percentage of purchases. Anna (cc) is aware and wants a quick plan.

Can your team triage? We need remediation options and an ETA — this is high priority for us.

— Jason
Infra Lead, Stellaris AI
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: infra@stellaris.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 09:27:35 -0400
Subject: Re: production: p95/p99 latency and 5xx burst on private VPC

Jason — thanks for the heads up and the logs. I’m escalating internally and pulling the on-call performance team into this thread.

Immediate asks while we triage:
- Can you confirm whether any config changes or new model deployments happened in the last 24 hours?
- If you can snapshot the request-size distribution and any recent rollout IDs that would help.

Marissa / Markus / Priyom — looping you in to lead the immediate investigation. Primary goals: surface the root cause (kernel mismatch, batching, or cache growth), provide a temporary mitigation that keeps customer traffic flowing (route-critical traffic to hosted fallback, alter batching), and an exec-facing summary for Anna.

I’ll coordinate an hourly sync and hold a 30m war room if needed.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com | +1-617-555-0142
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, infra@stellaris.ai
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 11:45:09 -0400
Subject: Re: production: p95/p99 latency and 5xx burst on private VPC

Quick diagnostic notes (initial):
- We pulled the runtime traces and metrics. There is significant KV cache growth on hot prefixes — cache size increased ~3x in the last 6 hours which is amplifying memory pressure and causing opportunistic eviction thrash.
- Observed a small but impactful kernel selection regression on the latest optimizer build for int8 paths: a new fused-attention kernel is being chosen for certain sequence-length buckets and is triggering longer kernel launch times on the customer's GPU type.
- Batching profiles show intermittent spikes in batch_size (from typical 8 to 24) due to a combination of recent client-side concurrency increases + our default burst batching policy. That increases tail latency when the new kernel path hits.

Short-term mitigations we recommend (can be applied as hotfix within 30-60 minutes):
1) Force the runtime to avoid the new fused-attention kernel for the affected model via runtime flag: --kernel-preference=stable
2) Lower max_batch_size from 32 -> 12 for the Stellaris VPC pool and disable optimistic burst batching for 2 hours
3) Increase KV cache eviction frequency to trim cold prefixes (ttl -> 2h) and enable immediate GC for inactive shards
4) Route 30% of critical traffic to our hosted fallback model (redwood-hosted/compat-stable-v2) while we stabilize — this preserves customer SLA for critical flows

I can push 1+2 as a config-only hotfix; will need a short downtime window (a few seconds of worker restarts). I'm standing by to coordinate with Stellaris infra.

—Marissa
Principal Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: anna.li@stellaris.ai, ceo@stellaris.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: infra@stellaris.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 12:10:22 -0400
Subject: Stellaris cluster incident — exec summary and proposed next steps

Anna / Leadership —

Summary: at ~08:45 UTC on 2026-06-21 Stellaris’ private VPC cluster experienced a sudden rise in tail latency and 5xxs, driven by KV cache bloat + a recent kernel path selection that increases launch latency on the customer's GPU type. Impact: p95 up ~4x, p99 higher, and throughput down ~35% for recommendation traffic. We estimate ~12k end-user requests affected in the 30-minute peak window.

Immediate plan (executive ask):
- Apply runtime flag to lock kernel selection (config-only) and reduce batching thresholds (technical fix) — timeline: 30–60m — minimal restarts required.
- Route critical recommendation flows (~30%) to Redwood hosted fallback for 3 hours during stabilization.
- Authorize 2 hours of Dedicated burst capacity to provide headroom if eviction/GC takes longer to converge. Estimated incremental cost: $1,800 for the window.
- Request a one-time credit of 20% on the impacted hour(s) due to SLA exposure while we remediate (this is a customer request).

Next steps: if you approve immediate action, we will implement the hotfix and provide an hourly status update. Postmortem and permanent tuning recommendations (kernel pinning, smarter kernel-selection heuristics per GPU family, KV cache heuristics) will be delivered within 72 hours.

Attachments: MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN_SNAPSHOT.pdf (sketch of tasks, owners, and timelines)

Priyom Das
Engineering Manager, Runtime Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: infra@stellaris.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: anna.li@stellaris.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 13:02:48 -0400
Subject: Re: Stellaris cluster incident — exec summary and proposed next steps

Thanks — that plan sounds good. Please proceed with kernel pin + batching limits and enable the hosted fallback for the critical recommendation route. We approve the 2 hour burst capacity. Anna asked that we get a short exec-friendly one-pager after the hotfix with clear customer impact numbers and the proposed credit.

We’ll wait for the first status update.

— Jason
Infra Lead, Stellaris AI
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: anna.li@stellaris.ai, infra@stellaris.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 08:30:00 -0400
Subject: Incident update: kernel pin + routing applied — p95 returned to baseline

Anna / Jason —

Update: the runtime flag was applied and batching limits lowered at 13:20 UTC 2026-06-21. We routed ~30% of critical recommendation traffic to the hosted fallback for three hours. By 14:05 UTC p95 had returned to pre-incident levels (~230ms) and throughput returned to expected levels. 5xxs dropped to baseline. We removed the temporary routing at 16:30 UTC after monitoring 2 hours of stable metrics.

Post-incident next steps (owner / ETA):
- Root cause report (Marissa / Markus) — 72 hours
- Permanent kernel-selection guard per GPU family (Runtime) — 2 weeks
- Improved KV cache TTL heuristics and metrics alert (Runtime/SRE) — 1 week
- Exec one-pager for Anna with impact numbers and proposed credit (Neha) — EOD today

We appreciate the quick approvals — will share the postmortem and next steps doc in the Drive link and HubSpot record linked in this thread.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
